subject: Clarifying evidence handover, notification windows, and subprocessor involvement
messages:
From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@optimabank.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: OptimaBank Legal <legal@optimabank.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: Request for incident timeline + evidence export authority

Diego —

We just received an alert from our SOC that suggests a potential exposure involving a small subset of our users who processed sensitive PII via your hosted API. Per our DPA (section 5.b), we need: (1) an initial acknowledgement and estimated timeline for notification, (2) a description of the scope of affected data (what types/IDs), and (3) the mechanism and authorization required to obtain forensics snapshots or exported evidence.

Attached is a completed request form (Optima_Inci_Request_Form.docx) with the initial questions filled out. We need to understand whether Redwood can meet a 72-hour preliminary notification window and whether Redwood will provide a sanitized export (redacted) or full raw logs to our retain-forensics partner (ForensicsCo).

Please loop in whomever on your side handles subprocessor cooperation — if any Redwood subprocessors need to be engaged to retrieve telemetry or stored artifacts, we need confirmation now. Also state whether cross-border transfer constraints (EU/UK data) will affect delivery timelines.

Sincerely,
Sara Jensen
Senior Counsel, OptimaBank
Sara.Jensen@optimabank.com
Attachment: Optima_Inci_Request_Form.docx

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@optimabank.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood-inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Request for incident timeline + evidence export authority

Sara — thanks for the heads up and for the completed form. I appreciate the clarity. Quick outline of our proposed approach so we can align expectations: 

- Acknowledgement: we can provide an initial acknowledgement within 24 hours of this email (this message will serve as the start of the clock).
- Preliminary notification window: our standard DPA language defines a preliminary notification milestone of "prompt" or "72 hours where feasible" for incidents with confirmed impact; however, the exact timing depends on the scope you require (full raw logs vs sanitized snapshot) and any legal authorization you can provide.
- Evidence export: we can produce a sanitized forensic snapshot (PII redacted/pseudonymized) ready for secure transfer within 7 calendar days for most cases. A full raw export (including KV cache and debug traces) may take longer (10+ days) and requires a signed export authorization and, depending on the data region, either EU-region extraction or additional legal justification for cross-border transfer.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a dynamic subprocessor roster at https://app.redwood-inference.com/subprocessors/list. If a subprocessor holds key artifacts, we will engage them under our DPA cooperation clause but will need a written authorization from Optima (signed form) to share exported data with your third-party forensics vendor.

Two asks from our side to avoid delays: (1) confirm the exact time range and sample identifiers you want included; (2) provide an executed authorization (DocuSign OK) naming ForensicsCo or a named internal custodian. I've attached our evidence export template (evidence_export_template.csv) and a one-line preliminary acknowledgement we can send to your stakeholders (prelim_ack.txt).

I'll loop in Naomi and Kimberly to confirm legal/transfer constraints and to start internal runbook coordination. If you'd like to hop on a short call today to align, I'm available 1–3pm PT.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Customer Operations — Redwood Inference
Attachments: evidence_export_template.csv, prelim_ack.txt

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@optimabank.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Request for incident timeline + evidence export authority

Sara / Diego —

Couple of legal points to clarify so we don't promise something we can't deliver under the DPA: 

1) Scope vs. notification timing: our DPA's incident clauses require us to provide "reasonably requested" information and reasonable assistance; we typically provide an initial technical summary within 72 hours and a follow-up with artifacts as they become available. Committing to a guaranteed 48-hour artifact delivery is not possible in all cases. We can, however, commit to a 24-hour acknowledgement + 72-hour initial technical summary, then a defined artifact delivery timeline (7–10 days) depending on export scope.

2) Subprocessor cooperation: Redwood will request cooperation from covered subprocessors. If a subprocessor holds the only copy of relevant telemetry, we will coordinate, but that cooperation may require the subprocessor's acceptance of a limited disclosure, and in some cases an NDA or data-handling addendum. Please confirm whether Optima will accept a sanitized snapshot rather than raw logs — that materially reduces subprocessor involvement.

3) Cross-border transfers & EU data: if the affected users are EU residents and the data is stored in an EU region, we prefer to transfer evidence out of the EU only after pseudonymization or under Standard Contractual Clauses / SCCs. If Optima needs raw data in the US, we will need a DPA amendment or an executed export authorization that references the applicable transfer mechanism.

4) Escrow/forensics vendor access: If you want ForensicsCo to access our environment directly (runbooks, snapshots), we will need a formal access agreement and scoped, time-bound credentials. Otherwise, we will deliver exports via encrypted S3 presigned URL or secure SFTP.

If you can confirm the points above (sanitized vs raw, time range, signed authorization), we'll move to runbook and subprocessor outreach immediately.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security — Redwood Inference

From: Michael Liu <michael.liu@forensicsco.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood-inference.com>, Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@optimabank.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Request for incident timeline + evidence export authority

Diego / Sara —

Quick technical intake from ForensicsCo so we can scope the work: 
- Desired time-range (UTC): please specify start/end timestamps (we prefer epoch ranges).
- Expected artifacts: request types (API request/response logs, KV cache dumps, model input payloads, server-side logs, app-level traces).
- Format: we prefer compressed JSONL or Parquet for large exports; if you can provide an initial CSV with sample record IDs, we'll validate mapping.
- KV cache: confirm whether the environment stores model-serving KV cache per request; retrieving it may require reaching into dedicated runtime nodes and involve our vendor liaison.

We can run a 30-minute runbook call to align on deliverables and transfer methods — available 2026-04-20 14:00–15:00 PT. Attached is a short onboarding checklist that helps us validate delivered artifacts (forensics-onboarding-checklist.pdf).

Regards,
Michael Liu
VP, Incident Response — ForensicsCo
Attachment: forensics-onboarding-checklist.pdf

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@optimabank.com>, Michael Liu <michael.liu@forensicsco.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood-inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Request for incident timeline + evidence export authority

All —

Thanks for the fast responses and the checklist. Summarizing agreed plan and next steps so everyone has a single source of truth: 

1) Acknowledgement: Redwood provided initial acknowledgement on 2026-04-18 within 24 hours.
2) Initial technical summary: Redwood will deliver a preliminary technical summary (suspected vectors, estimated affected record count, and list of artifact types available) within 72 hours (by 2026-04-21 EOD PT).
3) Artifact delivery: Redwood will provide a sanitized forensic snapshot (PII redacted/pseudonymized) containing API request/response logs and server-side traces as compressed JSONL via an encrypted S3 presigned URL within 7 calendar days (target delivery 2026-04-25). If Optima requires a raw export (including KV cache and model internal traces), that will be a separate delivery (estimated 10–14 days) and requires: (a) a signed export authorization naming ForensicsCo, (b) acceptance of transfer mechanism (SCCs or EU-region export plan), and (c) a scoped access agreement for subprocessors if they must be engaged.
4) Subprocessor engagement: Redwood will inventory which subprocessors hold relevant artifacts and will request their cooperation. If a subprocessor refuses or requires additional contractual terms, Redwood will inform Optima and propose mitigations.
5) Runbook call: Scheduled 2026-04-20 14:00 PT (ForensicsCo confirmed) to finalize time-ranges and artifact format.

Action items: 
- Optima: confirm whether sanitized snapshot is acceptable for the first delivery and provide signed authorization if a raw export is needed (link to DocuSign: https://docusign.com/optima-export-auth).
- ForensicsCo: confirm preferred compression/format (JSONL accepted) and validate onboarding checklist receipt.
- Redwood: Naomi to scope any DPA amendment language (if export/escrow/forensic access requested) and Kimberly to open subprocessor outreach ticket.

I'll attach the evidence export template and the internal runbook ticket id once created. If there are any schedule conflicts on the call, let me know and we'll pivot.

Best regards,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Customer Operations — Redwood Inference
Attachments: evidence_export_template.csv
